messages:
anya: Quick dump of the slot-slicing sim I ran overnight. Wanted feedback on whether this is worth a canary.

matt: awesome, paste the TL;DR first?

anya: TL;DR: slot-slice-first-fit (SSFF) increases packing efficiency on mixed-tenancy workloads from 69% -> 78% in our synthetic Q3 traffic, reclaims ~4.2% stranded GPU hours, but increases P99 latency for small interactive jobs by ~20ms. Tradeoff looks good for burstable tenants.

karen: can you share the workload mix and assumptions? especially the committed vs bursty split.

anya: sure — sim inputs: 65% bursty (short chat/generation), 25% committed long-running batches, 10% occasional large training. Sequence length distro matched prod: median 512, p95 2048. Seasonal multiplier: baseline x1, ramp to x1.38 in Q3 forecast window, and a holiday stress test at x1.65.

ryan: how is "slot-slice" defined here? sounds like fractional GPU packing?

anya: yeah — instead of coarse whole-GPU bins we allow up to 4 slices per GPU (configurable). Each slice carries a KV cache pointer and is scheduled with affinity. Evictions are soft: we use eviction-credits to avoid ping-pong. Basic config I used below:

```
# SSFF sim config
scheduler:
  mode: slot-slice
  slices_per_gpu: 4
  min_slice_size: 0.18  # fraction of a GPU (lets small jobs fit)
  eviction_credit_hours: 2h
  backfill_score:
    score_fn: "(tenant_usage/committed)^0.5 - frag_penalty*0.7"
    frag_penalty_weight: 0.7
```

anya: Key sim outputs (aggregate over 30-day simulated window):
- packing_efficiency: 78% (baseline: 69%)
- mean_gpu_utilization: 61% (baseline 53%)
- reclaimed_stranded_hours: 4.2% of total hours
- small-job_p99_infer_latency: 120ms (baseline 100ms)
- eviction_events_per_day: +0.9/day per 1k GPUs (mostly on heavy-batch tenants)
- tenant_fairness_index (weighted Jain): 0.82 (baseline 0.87)

matt: fairness index drop is concerning. Does that mean committed tenants see worse service?

anya: unpack — "weighted Jain" uses committed size as weight. Committed tenants lost about ~3% of throughput in peak windows because slices let bursty tenants occupy fractional slots. But their latency SLAs (tail) were preserved due to eviction credits routing long-running tasks to reserved micro-pools when score < threshold.

karen: can you show the micro-pool routing rule?

anya: rule snippet used in sim:
```
routing_policy:
  if tenant_committed_ratio >= 0.8 -> route: reserved_pool
  else if backfill_score >= 0.6 -> route: slice_pool
  else -> route: best_effort
```

anya: We also tested a hybrid: slices + periodic defrag (every 10min we opportunistically coalesce idle slices). That reduced fragmentation metric (empty_slot_ratio) from 0.28 -> 0.12 and recovered most fairness (index 0.86) at the cost of a small scheduling jitter.

ryan: nice. What's the cost/benefit for Dedicated customers? they buy reserved capacity; we can't erode that.

anya: Right — in the sim Dedicated trunks were mapped to reserved_pool and not eligible for slice backfill. The reclaimed hours were almost entirely from multi-tenant shared pools. For Dedicated we only recommend enabling slices inside a single tenant's fleet for intra-tenant binpacking.

matt: network/kv cache implications? KV cache per-slice sounds expensive memory-wise.

anya: it's basically a pointer & small descriptor per slice. For our runtime the extra state per slice is ~120KB, so 4 slices adds ~480KB per GPU — <1% of GPU host RAM on our instances. The bigger cost is the KV cache warmup on eviction; eviction_credits and periodic coalescing greatly reduce churn.

karen: did you run any sensitivity for holiday 1.65x? that usually breaks naive backfill.

anya: yes — under holiday stress packing efficiency still improved (74% vs 66% baseline) but eviction events spike ~x2. We added a temporary cap that reduces slices_per_gpu from 4->2 when regional load > 85%. That keeps P99 within SLA at cost of a few percent efficiency.

ryan: actionable ask? what do you want from infra team this week?

anya: want to run an internal canary on a small APAC cluster: spin up SSFF with slices_per_gpu=3 + periodic defrag, 2-week window. Goals: validate real-world latency tail, measure actual KV warmup cost, and confirm reclaimed hours. Need buy-in on metrics and a small quota to test (50 GPUs).

matt: +1. I'll own the canary infra provisioning. Assigning to me and @sre-bot to watch alerts.

karen: I'll prep a dashboard: per-tenant fairness, eviction rate, packing efficiency, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and stranded_hours metric.

ryan: can we add a canary kill-switch if tenant_fairness_index drops below 0.8 for >15m?

anya: yes — I'll add that to the rollout job. Also adding an automatic scale-down: if eviction_events_per_minute > 0.2 per GPU, we reduce slices_per_gpu by 1.

sre-bot: deploy ticket created: #DPL-4827. Canary cluster: apac-dev-run-ssff-01, GPUs requested: 50. Alerts: canary-fairness, canary-evictions, canary-latency.

matt: thanks. I'll schedule the deploy for Thurs 10:00 UTC. If no hot takes, I'll proceed and tag infra-oncall.

karen: quick note — document any tenant opt-outs. Legal asked us to make slices opt-in for enterprise contracts.

anya: good call. We'll add a tenant-level flag to disable slice backfill.

ryan: sounds good. excited to see real numbers. :rocket:

matt: ok moving to planning channel to coordinate the rollout steps.
